signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew vs Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 158.14, holding above its SMA20 and SMA50 cluster at 157.65/157.71 while capped below the SMA200 at 158.54. The 264bp OIS carry advantage favors USD via SOFR 3.87% over TONA 1.23%, sustaining long carry positioning alongside JPY speculative net shorts of −30,379 contracts. Options markets present an acute divergence, with 25-delta risk reversals printing a heavy put skew at −1.80 alongside an inverted vol risk premium where 1M ATM implied vol at 7.9% sits 1.8 points below 30-day realized volatility of 9.7%. This divergence indicates institutional accounts are aggressively accumulating downside hedges against intervention risk while spot grinds higher. A sustained breakout above the 160.00 threshold raises official intervention risk substantially. Trade bias: Neutral/fading USD/JPY on rallies; downside options skew warns against chasing carry near key resistance. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US CPI prints substantially above expectations, accelerating spot through 160.00 and forcing options hedges to liquidate.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Elevated Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1212, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1327 and SMA50 at 1.1492. Speculative positioning is stretched short with leveraged funds holding net −84,775 contracts, sitting in the 4th percentile of the 52-week historical distribution at z = −1.64 standard deviations. Hedging activity is expanding ahead of North American data, with 1M implied volatility at 6.5% running 2.2 points above 30-day realized volatility of 4.3%, signaling elevated options demand. Rates maintain a structural drag on the single currency, with Fed policy at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% yielding a 135bp nominal advantage for the dollar. Stretched short positioning against elevated options premium leaves the pair primed for a short-covering squeeze if dollar catalysts falter. Trade bias: Long EUR/USD on dips; oversold institutional positioning creates asymmetric upside squeeze vulnerability. Catalyst: US CPI report today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US core inflation accelerates above forecast, validating existing short positioning and breaking spot toward 1.1150.

signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NOK leads G10 performance over the 1-week window with a +0.760% average gain across 2 pairs, while EUR lags as the weakest peer at −0.298% across 9 pairs, generating a bilateral spread of 1.058%. Norges Bank policy at 4.50% carries a 185bp nominal policy rate premium over the ECB deposit rate at 2.65%, providing steady yield support to the Scandinavian currency. Domestic macroeconomic performance reinforces this spread, as the Economic Surprise Index for NOK prints at +13.1, supported by WTI crude stability at $94.7 per barrel. While EUR/NOK screens structurally cheap at z = −2.50 standard deviations below model fair value of 10.8514, fundamental momentum and yield differentials favor continued Norwegian outperformance. Trade bias: Long NOK/EUR; cross-rate yield advantage and macro momentum favor persistent divergence. Catalyst: Euro Area Industrial Production release today at 09:00 UTC. Risk: Sharp crude oil sell-off weakens NOK terms of trade and compresses the G10 performance spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Resistance at Moving Average Cluster
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3275, testing immediate technical resistance defined by the descending SMA20 at 1.3269, while remaining trapped below the major SMA50 and SMA200 cluster at 1.3431/1.3437. Rates markets provide minimal traction, with the OIS SONIA at 3.73% trailing SOFR at 3.87% by 14bp, while 2Y sovereign yield spreads between the UK and US remain flat at 0bp. CFTC speculative positioning shows leveraged funds holding a modest net long of +6,063 contracts after adding +11,440 contracts on the week, though 52-week percentile rank remains low at 8. Cross-asset signals warrant caution as MOVE bond volatility sits at the 94th percentile of its trailing year while VIX trades at the 15th percentile, reflecting underlying fixed income repricing risks. Without a clear yield incentive, spot remains constrained by upper technical boundaries. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD on rallies; overhead moving-average structure caps near-term upside. Catalyst: UK GDP m/m release today at 06:00 UTC. Risk: UK GDP delivers a substantial upside beat while BoE speakers signal immediate tightening, driving a clean technical break above 1.3300.
